messages:
jamie_sales: Quick sync  NovaCorp POC (Private in their VPC). They asked for a one-page preflight for their infra team: GPU driver/CUDA matrix, kube versions, required ports/egress, and how well get temporary access for field eng. Can we draft?

Dina_field_eng: Yep. Key items we need from them up front: node OS + kernel, GPU models (you said A100 PCIe + DGX?), whether cluster is managed (EKS) or self-managed, and if they allow outbound TLS to our control plane.

jamie_sales: Confirmed: EKS 1.24, A100 PCIe on dedicated nodes, small DGX for dev. They will allow outbound 443 but want a minimal list. No air-gap.

arun_infra: Recommended baseline: kernel >=5.10. NVIDIA driver >=525 for A100s; CUDA 11.8 is minimum, CUDA 12.1 recommended if they need latest perf kernels. Installer supports driver verification and will warn if incompatible.

katie_security: From security: we need an IAM role with least-privilege for the installer. Required permissions (read-only): ec2:DescribeInstances, iam:PassRole limited to the installer role, s3:GetObject for our artifacts (if using S3), kms:Decrypt/GenerateDataKey for customer KMS if they want remote model pulls. We'll include example policy snippet.

jamie_sales: Ports/egress short list pls. They want to hand to infra and be done.

arun_infra: Outbound: 443 to control plane + metrics endpoints (*.redwood-inference.com). If using Hosted pull we need S3 endpoints too. Inbound: kube-apiserver 6443 reachable from the jump host, node->node gRPC on 443 for runtime sharding. Docker/containerd socket must be reachable by installer (unix socket).

Dina_field_eng: For field-eng access: ask them to create a namespace `redwood-poc`, create a service account with `cluster-admin` only if they insist, otherwise we provide a minimal RBAC manifest. Provide an IRSA role if EKS so we can assume via AWS. We'll also request a temporary kubeconfig with a time-limited cert.

katie_security: Enterprise blocker: NovaCorp requires HSM-backed keys. They must provide KMS key ARN and grant our installer role kms:Encrypt/kms:Decrypt/kms:GenerateDataKey. Also require CloudTrail enabled + audit logs to a dedicated S3 with restricted access. Add NTP sync and validated TLS certs for any private registries.

deploybot: deploybot: installer-checklist results: 
- kernel_ok: true if >=5.10
- nvidia_module: present
- nvidia_container_toolkit: installed
- container_runtime: docker|containerd socket reachable
Log path: /var/log/redwood/installer.log
If any checks fail we output `node-check-fail` and a remediation hint.

Dina_field_eng: For CUDA smoke test we'll give them `rti-cuda-smoke.yaml` that runs a small NCCL all-reduce on 2 GPUs. Command to run after install: `kubectl -n redwood-poc run cuda-smoke --image=redwood/test-cuda:latest --restart=Never -- /bin/smoke-test`.

jamie_sales: Pricing question came up: POC cost if they run isolated GPU pool vs us managing Dedicated nodes?

Dina_field_eng: Short: Dedicated (reserved) = per-GPU-hour + managed infra cost. Private POC = one-time setup + monthly license + infra you pay. For a 2-week POC we usually invoice as usage + $X setup. I'll sync with finance for exact quote and send offline.

jamie_sales: Perfect. Can Dina/dina_field_eng drop a one-pager here I can forward to their infra lead? I'll mention the KMS HSM ask and the need for a temp kubeconfig.

Dina_field_eng: Will do. Drafting now: will include kernel/driver matrix, kube versions (min 1.22, recommended 1.24-1.27), ports, IAM policy example, smoke test steps, and how to create IRSA for field eng.

katie_security: I'll attach the S3 bucket policy snippet and the minimal KMS policy to include in the one-pager. Also note: require host os updates and DKMS if they plan driver recompile.

jamie_sales: Thanks team! Tagging NovaCorp infra when you post the one-pager. :white_check_mark:
